M3.title: Empire delegation and coordinated orders
M3.detail: Standing charters, muster points, army postings, cause-grouped alerts, bounded group postings/charters and the personal browser charter-template library are delivered. The 25 September saved-groups slice adds persistent canonical selections: Each realm can retain up to 24 named selection groups of owned land armies or hearths combined, with at most 128 members each. Ordinary canonical commands create, rename, replace or delete groups. A dedicated deterministic group counter preserves gameplay entity IDs, and observations expose only detached own groups to the viewer. Choosing a saved record issues no order; explicit Recall replaces the eligible selection on that registry tab, and posting/charter application remains a separate action. Permanent member loss is pruned at relevant successful lifecycle commands; empty named groups and temporarily embarked land armies are retained. Groups survive canonical save/reload, replay and campaign export/import. Genuine prechange rules-31 snapshots and archives retain their original bytes and seals; older saves gain fresh empty group registers. Rules 32 also repairs the existing 64-seat save limit for arcane research; earlier strict schemas stay frozen. Final publication verification passes 1,943 headless tests across 243 files, 20 affected Chromium journeys, 31 local production Pages journeys and 31 live Pages journeys. These are separate suite scopes, not additive test totals. Rules/save 32, unchanged content 015468d1. Theaters, patrol/escort roles, army-order templates, production sequences, broader governor decisions and combined mature-realm acceptance remain open.

roadmap.note: 6 of 23 catalogue items are complete and all 15 release gates remain open. Rules/save 32 adds canonical saved army/hearth selection groups to finite fleet supplies, group orders and the separate personal charter-template library. Acceptance-point totals are recomputed from the structured delivered/remaining catalogue bullets. Editorial regrouping changes these totals; they are not a fixed-scope completion percentage or release acceptance.
